Uruguay is easy to include in a South American journey with Argentina or Brazil, yet works equally well as a destination on its own. In Montevideo, allow time for city sights, markets, restaurants and the long waterfront promenade, then continue towards the coast or historic towns.

Colonia del Sacramento offers a more relaxed cultural stage. Its historic centre, seventeenth- and eighteenth-century buildings, museums and city lighthouse make it suitable for a day of its own or a stop between Montevideo and neighbouring countries.

For ocean relaxation, choose Punta del Este, Piriápolis, Cabo Polonio, La Paloma or other coastal areas. The itinerary can include boat trips, surfing, fishing and watching birds and animals.

In the northwest, add a visit to hot springs around Salto. Ada Tours can arrange a route through Uruguay combining cities, beaches, nature and gastronomic stops, or link it with Argentina and Brazil.

Venezuela combines the Caribbean coast, islands, Andes, savannas and regions of the Guiana Highlands. One trip can bring together beach relaxation, nature journeys, cities and visits to waterfalls.

Canaima National Park is one of the country's main destinations. A route here can focus on Canaima Lagoon, Sapo Falls, the Auyán-tepui massif and Angel Falls. The Orinoco Delta and Los Llanos savannas offer a different natural experience, with especially varied local wildlife.

Caracas suits the urban portion of the itinerary. Mérida opens the way into the Andes, while Santa Elena de Uairén is a starting point for trips through Gran Sabana and towards the tepuis.

For a seaside stay, choose the Los Roques archipelago or Margarita Island. Ada Tours can arrange a group or private journey in Venezuela or include the country on a combined Latin American trip.

## Coffee where it grows

In [Brazil](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/brazil/), coffee journeys lead to the historic fazendas of [Coffee Valley](/brazil/place/coffee-valley-rio-de-janeiro/). In [Colombia](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/colombia/), you can discover the farms of the Coffee Region or visit [Hacienda Coloma](/colombia/place/hacienda-coloma/) near Bogotá.

In [Costa Rica](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/costa-rica/), [Doka Estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/) can be combined with volcanoes and waterfalls. In [Panama](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/panama/), the coffee programme takes place in highland [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/).

## From coffee cherry to tasting

Farms demonstrate how beans are grown, harvested, processed and roasted. Visits differ: some focus on an estate's history, while others explain production and brewing methods. On the [El Ocaso coffee farm excursion](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/), the introduction to coffee production ends with a tasting. Check the exact programme and included services on your chosen tour page.

## A journey built around coffee or one day on a longer trip

You can devote most of your holiday to coffee or fit a plantation visit between cities and nature excursions. The [full coffee tour catalogue](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/) includes both formats. Tell us what appeals to you most: the history of coffee estates, production, tastings or a relaxing stay in a coffee region.

## Choose your travel format

River cruises, ocean voyages and expedition journeys are different formats. Compare duration, vessel, accommodation, shore landings and onshore activities using the description of each tour.

On expedition routes, the sequence of landings and crossings may depend on weather and local conditions. Exact arrangements are determined by the operator's itinerary.

## Every stop has its own story

You can devote your journey to ancient civilisations or combine archaeological sites with cities, museums and living traditions. The selection includes both cultural journeys and mixed itineraries with substantial historical programmes.

The duration and sequence of excursions are tailored to the chosen itinerary and your preferred pace.
